rows.stringValue: Updated 4 Sep: balanced diagnostic 180/180 verified; water exports checked. Open Next Up for home/work handoff; production decisions remain pending.
Completed: balanced VCF comparison and four water-export QA checks. GitHub handoff/2026-09-04 has reports, figures and scripts. No new overnight run or production replacement yet.
Pull origin main, then read handoff/2026-09-04/README.md. Reports, figures, scripts and context are bundled; ArcGIS data remain at home.
Use your own manuscript wording; no employer GIS license or another solver needed.
Review cost stability versus route-location uncertainty
180/180 verified; median absolute cost change 0.2213%; 49 route-years below 80% minimum directional 1 km overlap; no endpoint temporal sign reversals.
Report modeled structural connectivity, not validated movement. 80% is only a review trigger.
Interpret the newly verified water-class fractions
All four 11-band exports passed QA. Cross-tab covers 4866 missing cells: 715 persistently >=95% both-water, 14 both-land, 4137 other. Review spatial context next.
95% is descriptive, not an adopted exclusion rule. Do not equate NoData or wetlands with barriers.
Document final missing-data treatment, compare to candidate fallback, and identify impacted outputs before launching anything long.
Balanced candidate remains diagnostic; low/high and current flow are not approved by this comparison.
Corrected versioned CSV is in the handoff: old scores x21/23; 38-40 = 0.4090909. All ranks/ties unchanged.
Update production tables and manuscript consistently; no GIS solve needed.
Reconcile figure/table plan with verified evidence
Read bundled earlier figure/table plan and current README. Carry path-location uncertainty into priority interpretation; keep reference current flow distinct.
Final maps/priority revisions and predictive extension remain pending; do not label them complete.
Consolidated methodological choices, rationale, implementation, and caveats. This is the project’s decision memory, not a claim that provisional assumptions are final truth.
Use confirmed and likely cheetah range to define the analysis extent; exclude possible range from expanding the landscape.
Keeps the study focused on defensible occurrence evidence while still including likely movement space.
Range classes 3 and 2; 100 km buffer; class 1 retained only as contextual evidence.
The extent is an analytical boundary, not a claim that cheetahs cannot occur outside it.
Use a common 1 km equal-area grid for every resistance predictor and output.
Equal-area cells support comparable area, density, and cost calculations across southern Africa.
Africa Albers Equal Area Conic (ESRI:102022); identical 1,000 m cells; grid verified at 2,310 × 2,200.
Resampling must match data type; categorical layers require nearest neighbor.
Four-year spacing balances temporal comparison with dataset availability.
All time-varying inputs aligned to target years; nominal VIIRS 2012 uses the nearest 2013 observation.
The 2012 lights layer has a +1-year offset and must be disclosed.
Use VCF for vegetation-cover measurements and categorical land cover for classification context; land-cover classes do not independently add resistance.
The datasets answer different questions and adding both as penalties would risk double counting vegetation structure.
Six-class land cover is descriptive context; VCF tree, non-tree, and bare support vegetation interpretation.
Neither categorical land cover nor VCF is a causal resistance surface in the first model.
Do not include rainfall as an independent predictor in the first analysis.
The current question is movement resistance; rainfall would expand scope without a clear independent mechanism beyond available vegetation context.
CHIRPS step intentionally omitted, not failed.
Vegetation trends cannot be attributed to rainfall; rainfall variability was not independently controlled.
Use absolute change as the primary temporal result and proportional change as supplementary context.
Absolute change is stable when baseline values are small; proportional change can explode near zero.
Interval and 2012–2024 absolute differences for built-up, VCF, and flare-masked lights.
Proportional VCF maps remain exploratory rather than headline maps.
Apply a 5% baseline floor before calculating proportional VCF change.
Threshold review showed near-zero baselines created widespread unstable ratios.
All proportional VCF outputs rebuilt using the 5% baseline threshold.
Report threshold sensitivity and retain absolute maps as primary.
Mask gas flares before using VIIRS as a human-pressure indicator.
Flares can mimic settlements or infrastructure.
Dissolved 5 km flare buffer; one intersecting site; masked copies retained with untouched originals.
Document VIIRS export scale before reporting brightness magnitudes.
Represent roads with GRIP4 hierarchy and a 5 km neighborhood density surface.
Road effects extend beyond exact lines; the 5 km option produced a coherent regional exposure surface.
140,471 clipped GRIP4 features; hierarchy summaries; 5 km density selected.
Road density is a pressure proxy, not direct proof of avoidance or mortality.
Use mean slope as primary and maximum slope as supplementary context.
Mean slope represents prevailing movement cost; maximum slope can overemphasize isolated rugged cells.
Native 30 m SRTM aggregated to 1 km; resistance 1 through 10°, linear to 10 at 30°, capped.
Transferred form is provisional; run an alternate terrain sensitivity.
Use GLW4 2020 cattle, goats, and sheep as a static livestock-exposure index.
Livestock indicates pastoral exposure and associated people/fences but is not itself a conflict observation.
Three aligned 1 km layers combined after redundancy review.
Call it exposure, not conflict; static 2020 data cannot represent change.
Use correlation as screening and exclude VCF from the first weighted resistance model.
Strong VCF compositional correlations and cattle–goat correlation warn against separate penalties.
VCF tree–bare ρ=-0.877; non-tree–bare ρ=-0.836; cattle–goats r=0.774.
Correlation does not prove ecological interchangeability or causation.
Weight built-up, flare-masked lights, and road density equally within human pressure.
No defensible species-specific evidence supports privileging one proxy.
Equal weighting is a transparent starting hypothesis requiring sensitivity testing.
Use 0.50 human pressure, 0.30 livestock exposure, and 0.20 terrain.
Working hypothesis: human pressure dominates broad-scale resistance while livestock and terrain still matter.
Weighted standardized components; VCF and land cover remain context.
Weights are hypotheses, not fitted biological truth; compare alternatives.
Model fences as scenarios because reference data are incomplete.
Known veterinary fences may strongly constrain movement, but locations and permeability are unevenly documented.
Use finite-crossing documented-only and documented-plus-uncertain Kruger scenarios.
Prevents invented transversal paths without claiming the entire boundary is impermeable.
Fenced 621.85 km; open 240.95 km; uncertain 286.31 km; constrained multiplier 25.
Reference lines are not proof of current condition at every segment.
Define cores at density ≥0.51 cheetahs/100 km² and retain patches ≥500 km² with 8-neighbor connectivity.
Identifies meaningful-use areas while avoiding tiny fragments as equivalent cores.
23 cores; 246,654 km² total; smallest 506 km²; largest 99,673 km².
Report threshold trade-offs and test alternatives.
Keep the same core areas across temporal resistance comparisons.
Changing cores and resistance together would confound interpretation.
Fixed primary cores are endpoints for all snapshots and scenarios.
Results show changing resistance between fixed reference cores, not shifting populations.
Use a 3-nearest-neighbor graph plus a minimum spanning tree.
Limits implausible all-to-all routing while ensuring every core remains connected.
45 candidate links among 23 cores; MST contributes 22 connectivity links.
Candidate pairs are not corridors; cost-distance analysis determines pathways.
Use country absolute-change summaries descriptively, not causally.
Administrative summaries communicate where change occurs without claiming borders caused it.
Eight countries; 160 rows across absolute built, VCF, and masked-light changes.
Country means can conceal local heterogeneity and should accompany maps.
Combine built-up, roads, livestock exposure and nighttime lights into one anthropogenic-pressure component; keep terrain separate.
Livestock presence usually implies pastoral human activity, so treating livestock as fully independent from human pressure would overstate conceptual independence.
Top level: anthropogenic 80%, terrain 20%. Within anthropogenic: built 30%, roads 30%, livestock 30%, lights 10%.
Weights are hypotheses; livestock exposure is not direct evidence of conflict and nighttime lights is a weak proxy in dark rural areas.
Compare the primary anthropogenic weights with equal and infrastructure-dominant alternatives.
The literature supports cumulative pressure surfaces but does not provide uniquely correct cheetah-specific weights.
Equal: 25% each. Infrastructure-dominant: built 35%, roads 35%, livestock 20%, lights 10%. Terrain remains 20% at the top level.
Sensitive links must be reported as model-dependent rather than hidden by a single preferred surface.
Treat 34 core pairs as weight-robust and 11 as weight-sensitive under the tested alternatives.
Robustness across plausible assumptions is stronger evidence than agreement with one arbitrary weighting.
Ninety comparisons across 45 pairs and two alternatives; 34 pairs stable under both, 11 sensitive under at least one.
Robust here means robust to these two tested weight sets, not to every possible model structure.
Recalculate only primary paths that cross cells whose resistance increases under a fence scenario.
Adding nonnegative cost outside an unchanged primary path cannot make an alternative route cheaper than that unchanged path; screening avoids redundant runs.
Five affected pairs: 1–13, 1–17, 9–13, 13–17 and 27–30. Forty unaffected paths are carried forward per scenario.
After rerouting around KAZA fences, Kruger assumptions can still affect the new route, so all four scenarios are evaluated for the five links.
Retain four complete 45-link networks: fence main, fence near-barrier, Kruger documented and Kruger conservative.
A complete network per assumption allows direct link-level and network-level comparison without treating incomplete fence mapping as truth.
All 5 affected links succeeded in every scenario; 40 unaffected links were preserved. Four complete scenario networks assembled.
Reference fence geometry is incomplete and uncertain; results describe scenario sensitivity, not verified present-day permeability.
Extend the analysis to 2030, 2040 and 2050 under conservation/low-growth, continuation and high-development scenarios.
The project can support prospective conservation planning if forecast assumptions are explicit and externally grounded.
Use published projections where available; use historical extrapolation only when no defensible projection exists. Keep the same 23 cores.
Nighttime lights should not be blindly extrapolated because of saturation and proxy limitations.
Validate forecasting logic by using 2012–2020 to predict held-out 2024 before projecting beyond 2024.
A hindcast tests whether the model reproduces an observed future state rather than only fitting the past.
Compare predicted and observed 2024 predictors/resistance; also compare routes with independent GPS, occurrence, genetic or road-mortality evidence where legally available.
External biological data may be spatially incomplete, proprietary or collected at a different scale.
Keep robust importance, future threat and intervention leverage as separate scores, then assign Protect, Defend, Restore or Mitigate-barrier actions.
Separating value, threat and tractability prevents a single opaque index from hiding why a place is prioritized.
Protect = robust; Defend = likely deterioration; Restore = degraded former connection; Mitigate = localized fence/road/development pinch point.
Action labels are decision support, not proof that an intervention will succeed.
Frame results as temporally comparative, scenario-based structural connectivity among fixed cheetah cores—not verified animal movement corridors.
The project is novel in its combination of retrospective change, fixed cores, explicit fence uncertainty, robustness testing and conservation actions, but cheetah connectivity models already exist.
Working framing: changing anthropogenic pressure and uncertain fence permeability may alter modeled pathways among fixed southern African cheetah cores.
Literature review and complete LCP workflow
Avoid claiming the first cheetah connectivity model or equating least-cost paths with realized dispersal or gene flow.
Completed 180/180 pair-year comparisons and independent receipt review.
Check revised VCF inputs before any production replacement.
45 fixed pairs x4 years; 84 source checkpoints; no extra solver during review.
Balanced diagnostic only; not corrected low/high or final current flow.
Separate cost/trend stability from exact path-location stability.
Small optimized cost changes can accompany substantial displacement.
Median absolute cost difference 0.2213%, max 1.9625%; no 45-pair temporal sign reversals. 49/180 below 80% min directional 1km overlap; 29 pairs, including 21/32 prior eligible pairs.
80% overlap is descriptive, not biological or automatic priority exclusion. No observed-movement validation.
Use standard undirected EDGE normalization; propagate versioned correction later.
Old node denominator 231 should be edge denominator 253 for 23 nodes.
All45 scores x21/23; ranks/ties unchanged. Top38-40 =0.4090909, not0.4480519. Independently checked NetworkX3.6.
Production tables/manuscript not yet changed. Fixed unweighted centrality is structural, not ecological validation.
Four exports received and QA passed; final missing-data policy still open.
Distinguish native classified-area fractions from old cell-center flags.
95% is a descriptive bin, not exclusion policy. Same-product LW/LC agreement is not independent validation; fractions are not measured inundation.
Do not automatically rerun everything or promote candidate results.
No candidate path traverses fallback cells;8 touch <95% valid common coverage.
Increasing costs only on unused cells preserves an optimum under identical graph/endpoint conventions; lowering costs may create alternatives.
Conditional computational result, not biological justification; does not cover current flow, other weights or other modified cells.
Resume from the dated GitHub bundle and Next Up; preserve completed runs.
Avoid repeating analyses or losing context between computers.
Work: review reports/write own paper. Home: interpret fractions, finalize policy, assess rerun scope, propagate correction. No production edits today.
Large GIS datasets/credentials are not in bundle; ArcPy scripts require home data. Older forecast/figure plans are not completed outputs.
